medium.title: Oil Prices Dive as More Tankers Move Through Strait of Hormuz
medium.summary: Crude oil prices fell sharply, heading for steep weekly losses as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz resumed at greater volume, alleviating earlier supply disruption fears. A cargo vessel was struck near Oman — with reported Iranian involvement — but oil flows have continued largely uninterrupted. Analysts are also flagging anticipated oversupply conditions, adding further downward pressure on prices, with Saudi Aramco resuming loading operations as a positive supply signal. For INR traders, this is a constructive development: India is a major crude oil importer, and lower oil prices typically reduce the current account deficit, ease imported inflation, and provide support for the Rupee. A sustained decline in Brent/WTI could reduce India's import bill meaningfully and lessen pressure on RBI to defend INR. Watch whether this supply easing is sustained or reversed by geopolitical escalation near Hormuz.

medium.title: Gold Gains as Dollar Weakens; Still on Track for Fourth Straight Weekly Loss
medium.summary: Gold prices edged modestly higher on Friday, supported by a softer U.S. dollar and slightly tempered expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes following the latest U.S. inflation print. However, gold remains on course for a fourth consecutive weekly decline, having hit a seven-month low earlier in the week, reflecting the broader headwind from elevated global interest rates. For INR and Indian markets, a weaker USD is broadly supportive of Rupee stability and could encourage EM capital inflows. Easing U.S. rate hike expectations, if confirmed, would reduce the interest rate differential pressure that has weighed on INR. Gold's direction also matters for India's import demand — sustained weakness in gold prices could modestly trim India's import bill, offering marginal CAD relief.
